title: Problem Overview
content:
**Erdős Problem #665** asks: can pairwise balanced designs always have blocks close to √n in size?

A PBD on {1,...,n} is a collection of blocks where every pair appears in exactly one block, with block sizes between 2 and n-1.

**The question**: Does h(n) = O(1), where h(n) measures how far below √n the smallest block must be?

**Status**: OPEN. The answer depends on projective plane existence and prime gap bounds.
mathContext: See annotation content for formal details of problem overview

title: Pairwise Balanced Design
mathContext: PBDs generalize projective planes and affine planes. When all blocks have the same size k, it's called a (n, k, 1)-design.

title: The Erdős Question and h(n)
content:
**ErdosQuestion**: ∃ C, ∀ n ≥ 10, ∃ PBD with all blocks > √n - C.

**h(n)** (axiomatized): the minimum deficiency — the smallest value k such that a PBD exists with all blocks > √n - k.

**h_spec**: h(n) is the infimum of deficiencies over all PBDs on n points.

The question reduces to: is h(n) bounded?
mathContext: See annotation content for formal details of the erdős question and h(n)

title: Erdős-Larson Bound (1982)
content:
**erdos_larson_bound (axiom):** h(n) ≤ C · n^{1/2-c} for some c > 0.

This is the best unconditional upper bound. It shows h(n) grows slower than √n, but doesn't resolve whether h(n) is bounded.

The gap between O(1) (if true) and n^{1/2-c} is enormous.
mathContext: The exponent 1/2-c means h(n) = o(√n), so blocks can be made close to √n, but we don't know if the gap can be made constant.

title: Projective Plane Connection
content:
**shrikhande_singhi (axiom):** PBDs with blocks ≥ √n - c embed in projective planes.

**prime_power_planes_implies_unbounded (axiom):** If all projective plane orders are prime powers, then h(n) is unbounded — giving a NEGATIVE answer.

This is the key obstacle: projective planes of non-prime-power order (if they exist) would enable more flexible constructions.
mathContext: A projective plane of order q has q²+q+1 points and lines of size q+1. The only known orders are prime powers. Whether non-prime-power orders exist is one of the most famous open problems in combinatorics.

title: Prime Gap Connection
content:
**largestPrimeGap n (axiom):** H(n) = max gap between consecutive primes ≤ n.

**h_correlates_with_prime_gap (axiom):** h(n) ≤ C · H(n). Design deficiency is bounded by the largest prime gap.

**cramers_conjecture (axiom):** H(n) ≤ C(log n)². If true, gives h(n) = O((log n)²), much better than n^{1/2-c} but still not O(1).
mathContext: The connection arises because near-optimal PBDs use affine planes AG(2,q) for primes q ≈ √n. The largest gap between such primes determines h(n).

title: Special Case Constructions
content:
**perfect_square_case (axiom):** For n = q² with q prime, the affine plane AG(2,q) gives a PBD with all blocks of size exactly q = √n. Perfect result — h(q²) = 0.

**near_square_case (axiom):** For n = q² + k (k ≤ q), blocks of size ≥ q-1 are achievable. The deficiency is at most 1.
mathContext: See annotation content for formal details of special case constructions

title: Summary Theorem
content:
**erdos_665_summary (proved from axioms):**

Combines three key results:
1. Erdős-Larson: h(n) ≤ n^{1/2-c} unconditionally
2. Prime power planes ⟹ h(n) unbounded (negative answer)
3. h(n) correlates with largest prime gap H(n)

Proved by: `⟨erdos_larson_bound, prime_power_planes_implies_unbounded, h_correlates_with_prime_gap⟩`
